newsitem.title: POLAND: Zloty trade unaffected by foreign T-bill buying.
newsitem.headline: Zloty trade unaffected by foreign T-bill buying.

text.p: The zloty was unaffected by some $60 million worth of foreign purchases of Polish T-bills on Monday as some investors already had zlotys on their accounts and others sold currency after market close, dealers said.
"The bulk of today's T-bill purchases has already gone through the market after the fixing," one dealer at a major bank here said.
Dealers said the zloty was unlikely to be under upward pressure tomorrow either, and was likely to keep well below the 2.5 percent from the central bank parity rate resistance.

The zloty closed just up at 2.53/2.43 percent from the trading band centre, against Friday's close at 2.45/2.41 percent. It was at 3.1525/45 to the dollar, down from 3.1515/25 on Friday and at 1.8515/35 to the mark, down from 1.8335/50.

Dealers also said that the so far steady inflow of foreign investment into Polish paper now turned into two-way trade, as some investors apparently took profits after the central bank made it clear the zloty could only weaken in the near-term.
"Since the NBP placed a cap on zloty gains some short-term investors may be taking profits as the yield itself is not good enough," said Wojciech Kowalczyk of Bank Handlowy SA.

On the money market call money rates stayed around 22.0 percent as the market apparently found equilibrium around the National Bank of Poland's 14-day reverse repo rate of 22.15 percent and the 273-day NBP-bill yield of 22.00 percent.
O/N depos closed at 21.80/22.10 percent, flat from opening, and T/N at 21.95/22.20 pct, also stable, after the NBP refrained from an open market operation on Monday.
